1.fullVerseTranslation: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], the Abundance.

words.explanation: Particle of emphasis (harf tawkeed) acting as a nasib/nasikha, requiring the accusative case (mansub) for the following clause. The suffix 'na' is the detached pronoun of majesty (plural of respect).

Verb in the past tense (fi'l madi), Form IV, first-person plural, acting as the predicate of 'inna'. The 'ka' suffix is the second-person masculine singular object pronoun (maf'ul bihi) in the accusative state.
Definite noun in the accusative state (mansub) as the direct object of the verb 'a'taynaka'. It functions as a masdar or hyperbolized description of the overflow of goodness given to the Prophet.

2.fullVerseTranslation: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.

words.explanation: The 'fa' is a consequential particle (fa-sababiyya). 'Ṣalli' is an imperative verb (fi'l amr) derived from the root ṣ-l-w, with the final weak consonant removed due to the jussive nature of the command (majzum).
The 'li' is a preposition (harf jarr) indicating direction/devotion. 'Rabb' is the noun in the genitive case (majrur) due to the preposition. 'Ka' is the possessive pronoun suffix.
The 'wa' is a coordinating conjunction (harf 'atf). 'Inḥar' is an imperative verb (fi'l amr) in the second-person masculine singular, signifying the act of ritual slaughter for Allah alone.

3.fullVerseTranslation: Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.

words.explanation: Particle of emphasis (harf tawkeed), requiring the following noun to be in the accusative state (mansub).
Active participle (ism fa'il) in the accusative case (mansub) as the ism of 'inna'. The 'ka' suffix is the genitive object pronoun.
Personal detached pronoun used here for emphasis (damir fasl) to strengthen the assertion and specify the subject of the predicate.
Definite noun acting as the predicate (khabar) of 'inna' in the nominative case (marfu'). It denotes the one deprived of good or legacy.
